In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of the chemical modification of the anticodon on the aminoacylation reaction.
the effect of specific base modifications on tRNA structure and function.
the role of tRNA in the initiation of translation in prokaryotes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of the 6-sulfonic acid group at position 6 of uridine 37 in the anticodons of tRNAfmet alters the kinetic parameters of the aminoacylation reaction.
modification of U37 in the tRNAfMet anticodon by bisulfite alters the kinetic parameters of methionine aminoacylation of this tRNA by E. coli methonyl-tRNA synthetases.

the presence of an uridine/bisulphite adduct at the anticodon base in tRNAfMet alters the kinetic parameters of methionyl-tRNAMet synthetase, resulting in decreased affinity and a reduction in the rate of aminoacylation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the kinetic parameters for tRNA aminoacylation can be altered by modification of a single base within the tRNA molecule.

the kinetic constants for aminoacylation by methionyl-tRNASer, methionyl-tRNAThr, and methionyl-tRRNAVal were not altered by the presence of the diastereoisomeric bisulfite adduct at U18 in either the dihydrouracil loop (positions 18, 18') or the variable loop (positions 48, 48').
modification of a specific base in the anticodon of tRNAfmet alters the kinetic parameters (Km and Vmax) for aminoacylation by E. coli methonine-tRNA synthetases.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the anticodon base is involved in a critical interaction with the enzyme during the aminoacylation of the tRNAfMet, an interaction which is disrupted by the presence of the bisulfite adduct at the U37 site.
the anticodon is a major determinant of tRNAfmet aminoacylation.
the kinetic parameters of aminoacylation of E. coli formylmethonine transfer RNA by methionyl tRNA synthetase are altered by the presence of a bisulfite-modified uridine in the anticodon.
